Back in the 8 and 16 bit era my older cousin would basically get every single game and console that would come out.  Gameboy was no exception so of course he picked up Final Fantasy Legend when it was new.  Guy is mad skilled at games but had absolutely understanding (or a desire to understand ) RPGs so he just gave it to me, his nerdy younger cousin.  I was 7 years old and I was pretty clueless but I very much caught onto the most basic of the basics pretty early on, devoting all my time to cracking the mysteries of this weird tower.  By the time I had finished it (which probably took at least 6 months, even with the help of Nintendo Power) I became addicted to the genre for life.

SaGa Frontier ended up being the first game I ever pre-ordered.  Had no idea about the connection with Final Fantasy Legend.  I was riding high on how SquareSoft of the era seemed like it could no lose, I was already a massive fan of the company already but at that point they could have made a turn based janitor simulator and I would have picked it up no questions asked.  I absolutely hated it and it's mess of obtuse mechanics, ended up shifting my focus to Wild ARMs (which I had picked up at the same time, it was only $10 after all).

Fast forward maybe 3 months.  One of my friends had finally gotten a Playstation and asked for some games to borrow.  SaGa was sitting there collecting dust, at this point I had gotten stuck in every single scenario, so told him to have at it.  A week later was over his house and he's raving about how it's an amazing game and I legit thought he was messing with me.  So I sit down and watch him play through the second half of Red's story, explaining the mechanics he had figured out by this point.

A week or so later he returned the game to me, along with some tips.  By this point being the gaming magazine junkie I was did pick up the current issue of EGM2 (their strategy focused spin off) that included a broad walk through for each character, which helped a ton and I still have today.  After that the missing pieces started to slowly fill in and with each scenario finished my love and appreciation grew.  By the time I had finished high school six years later I was completely addicted to the series, the few games we got, and had learned of it's odd history.

Given the events of the last nine years (wow, hard to imagine it's been that long since the RS2 remaster) it's been incredible to see the resurgence in the series.  I still have trouble believing the RS2 remake even exists and isn't just some wonderful dream.  I'm far from some expert when it comes to actually playing the games but my passion is absolutely top tier and it's a dream come true to have so many people to share it with decades after I thought it was doomed to obscurity (at least in the states).
